newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds near static in becalmed summer market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds near static in becalmed summer market.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped marginally in a quiet summer market on Monday, following the general European trend with the yield curve expected to continue flattening.

"Short-term bonds are being dragged down by Germany, but there is solid buyer interest in long Danish paper. The yield curve is flattening here a touch more than abroad and this tendency will probably continue," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.06 point from the start at 114.01, yielding 5.87 percent at 1035 GMT.
The forchcoming tone-setting seven percent 2007 bond, due to take over as benchmark on September 1, was 0.05 point lower at 106.91, with yield at 6.07 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 benchmarks was around one billion and 600 million crowns respectively.

The 2006's September future fell 0.06 point to 113.54 with 25 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.15 point to 92.50. The crown traded at a virtually unaltered 3.8071 per mark, while the 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 49.
